title: FBR Digital Invoicing in Pakistan: 2026 Guide & Costs
excerpt: FBR digital invoicing is mandatory for many Pakistani businesses in 2026. Here's who's required, how the system works, what it costs, and the penalties for non-compliance.
content:
What Is FBR Digital Invoicing?

FBR digital invoicing — also called FBR e-invoicing — is the Federal Board of Revenue's mandatory real-time invoice transmission system. Under the rules, a sales-tax-registered person within scope must issue every sales invoice through an FBR-integrated system. The moment the invoice is generated, the system transmits the data to the FBR, which returns a unique Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a QR code. The buyer's copy of the invoice — paper or digital — must carry both.

The system replaces traditional invoice books and stand-alone billing software for businesses inside the mandate. It pulls Pakistan's sales tax compliance closer to the model already running in India (e-invoicing under GST), Saudi Arabia (ZATCA), and the UAE (FTA digital tax invoices). The goal is to close the gap between what a seller declares on a return and what actually changed hands at the till.

FBR digital invoicing is operated through the FBR's integrated portal infrastructure (built on the IRIS stack at iris.fbr.gov.pk) and authorised licensed integrators. Businesses connect either directly with the FBR system or through one of the approved integrators.

Who Needs to Use FBR Digital Invoicing in 2026?

The mandate applies to specific categories of sales-tax-registered persons, brought into scope through Statutory Regulatory Orders (SROs) issued by the FBR. The categories that have been notified so far include:

  • Tier-1 retailers — large retail businesses meeting the criteria in Section 2(43A) of the Sales Tax Act 1990 (annual electricity bill above the threshold, retail outlets meeting size or staffing tests, or retailers operating in a national or international chain)
  • Registered persons making supplies to government departments — federal, provincial, autonomous bodies, or PSEs
  • Manufacturers and importers in scheduled sectors — categories like fast-moving consumer goods, electronics, beverages, and select industrial items as specified in successive SROs
  • Wholesalers, distributors, and dealers in notified product categories
  • Businesses meeting prescribed turnover thresholds — the threshold is revised periodically and tightens with each SRO

If your business doesn't fall in any current category, you should still pay attention. The FBR has expanded the FBR digital invoicing scope steadily since the framework launched, and the trajectory points toward eventual coverage of all sales-tax-registered persons. Monitoring SRO releases and being implementation-ready before your category is notified beats scrambling after a deadline.

Not sure where you stand? Run a quick check on your FBR registration status, then look at the most recent SRO list on the FBR website, or ask us to confirm whether your business is in scope today.

How FBR Digital Invoicing Works — Step by Step

From a business's perspective the FBR digital invoicing flow has five stages. Once the integration is live, most of these are invisible — the system handles them automatically. Here's what happens behind every transaction:

  1. Invoice generation. The seller's billing system creates an invoice with the standard fields: buyer details, item description, HS code, sales tax amount, and any further taxes.
  2. Real-time transmission. The integrated billing software sends the invoice payload to the FBR via a secure API call. This happens in milliseconds.
  3. IRN and QR generation. The FBR validates the data, issues an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), and returns a QR code that encodes the IRN, seller STRN, total, and date.
  4. Invoice finalisation. The seller's system embeds the IRN and QR code on the invoice — both on screen for digital invoices and in print on physical receipts. Without them, the invoice is not legally compliant.
  5. Buyer-side traceability. The buyer can scan the QR code or look up the IRN through FBR digital invoicing verification on the FBR portal to confirm the invoice is genuine and the input tax claim is supportable.

Behind the scenes, the FBR is now matching transmitted invoices against the sellers' monthly sales tax returns automatically. Mismatches are flagged for audit — which is why getting the integration correct matters more than just getting it installed.

The Legal Basis: Sales Tax Act 1990 and the Relevant SROs

The FBR digital invoicing mandate sits on top of the Sales Tax Act 1990. The Act gives the FBR the power to prescribe the form, manner, and method of invoicing for any class of registered persons. The actual scope and timelines are then operationalised through SROs — a few of the relevant ones:

  • The general framework establishing real-time invoice transmission for Tier-1 retailers
  • Sector-specific SROs that bring additional industries into scope
  • Procedural SROs covering the technical specifications, integrator licensing, and penalty mechanisms

Specific SRO numbers change as the FBR amends and re-issues them. The practical takeaway: don't rely on a single SRO reference you read two years ago — check the current list when you start your implementation. Pakistan's tax authority publishes them at fbr.gov.pk.

What Happens If You Don't Comply with FBR Digital Invoicing?

Non-compliance with the FBR digital invoicing mandate carries real cost — and not just the headline penalty. The Sales Tax Act 1990 provides a layered enforcement framework:

  • Direct penalties. Section 33 of the Sales Tax Act 1990 includes specific penalties for failure to issue invoices in the prescribed manner. These start in the low five-figure range per default and escalate for repeat offenders.
  • Disallowance of input tax for buyers. An invoice that doesn't carry a valid IRN and QR code may not support an input tax claim by the buyer. This is the bigger commercial risk: your customers stop accepting your invoices because their input tax is at stake.
  • De-registration risk. Persistent non-compliance can lead to suspension of the seller's sales tax registration — meaning every subsequent invoice you issue is invalid until the suspension is lifted.
  • Audit selection. The FBR's risk-based audit engine flags non-integrated registered persons in scoped categories. An audit costs you in time, in professional fees, and in possible re-assessment of past returns.

The biggest hidden cost isn't the FBR fine — it's the customer attrition when buyers move to a compliant supplier so they don't lose their input tax claim.

How Much Does FBR Digital Invoicing Cost in Pakistan?

The cost of FBR digital invoicing in Pakistan splits into three buckets. Knowing what each one is helps you budget accurately and choose the right implementation path:

1. Government & portal fees

The FBR doesn't charge a per-invoice fee for the real-time transmission itself. The portal access is free for registered persons. What you do pay for, indirectly, is integrator licensing if you go through an authorised licensed integrator (LI) — those fees vary and are usually rolled into the integrator's service plan.

2. Integration cost

The one-off integration cost depends on your existing setup:

  • If you have no billing software, you adopt one that's already FBR-ready — the integration is bundled in the subscription.
  • If you have an existing POS or invoicing tool, you pay either a development cost (PKR 50,000–500,000+ depending on complexity) or a licensing cost from the vendor for the FBR-ready connector.
  • If you have a custom-built system, you pay your own developers for the API integration plus testing.

3. Ongoing service fees

Most businesses opt for a managed FBR digital invoicing service rather than running everything in-house. The going rate is roughly:

  • PKR 3,000–6,000/month for low-volume businesses (up to ~50 invoices/month)
  • PKR 8,000–20,000/month for mid-volume businesses
  • Custom quotes for high-volume retailers and chains

Our own FBR digital invoicing service at Fair Tax International runs on these tiers — a one-time onboarding fee plus a fixed monthly subscription that covers transmission, IRN management, reconciliation against your books, and any rectification handling. There's no separate per-invoice charge.

The internal-time cost most businesses miss

Even with a managed service, the first month involves your finance team re-mapping invoice templates, testing the connector against existing POS hardware, training cashiers, and reconciling the first batch of FBR-transmitted invoices against the books. Budget 20–40 staff hours for the cutover. After the first month, the workload drops to near zero.

Three Ways to Implement FBR Digital Invoicing

You have three practical paths. Each suits a different stage of business size and technical maturity:

Option 1: Direct integration with FBR

Your developers connect your billing software directly with the FBR API. You manage authentication, error handling, retries, and IRN reconciliation in-house. This works for businesses with an internal IT team, deep ERP investment, and the appetite to maintain the integration as the FBR specification evolves.

Pros: No third-party dependency, lowest ongoing cost.
Cons: Highest upfront effort, ongoing maintenance burden every time the FBR updates the API.

Option 2: Adopt FBR-ready accounting/POS software

Switch to a platform that already includes FBR digital invoicing as a feature — the connector ships built in. The trade-off is you might need to migrate from your current system, retrain staff, and accept the platform's feature set.

Pros: Out-of-the-box compliance, no custom integration.
Cons: Migration cost, vendor lock-in.

Option 3: Managed FBR digital invoicing service

A specialist firm handles the FBR portal integration, monitors transmissions, manages IRN issues, reconciles against your books each month, and represents you in any FBR query about invoice transmission. You keep your existing billing software where possible.

Pros: Lowest internal effort, single point of accountability, fastest to go live (often within one to two weeks).
Cons: Recurring monthly cost.

For most small-to-mid Pakistani businesses, Option 3 is the cheapest in total cost of ownership over a 24-month horizon — once you factor in internal time, error costs, and the FBR specification churn.

Common Questions About FBR Digital Invoicing

Is FBR digital invoicing mandatory for all sales-tax-registered persons?

Not yet. As of 2026, the mandate covers specific categories notified by the FBR — Tier-1 retailers, government suppliers, and businesses in scheduled sectors. The scope is expanding with each SRO, and full coverage of registered persons is the trajectory.

Can I issue an FBR digital invoice without an IRN?

No. Without a valid IRN and QR code from the FBR system, the invoice doesn't meet the prescribed form under the Sales Tax Act 1990. The buyer cannot use it to support an input tax claim, and you remain exposed to penalties under Section 33.

What if my internet goes down or the FBR portal is unavailable?

The FBR system supports a fallback mechanism — most integrators queue invoices locally and transmit as soon as connectivity returns. If you're evaluating an integrator or service provider, ask specifically about their offline-queue handling.

Do I need to issue digital invoices to walk-in customers without an STRN?

Yes — the FBR digital invoicing mandate applies to every sales transaction by a registered person inside scope, regardless of whether the buyer is registered. The invoice still gets transmitted; the buyer field simply records that the buyer is unregistered.

How is FBR digital invoicing different from the POS integration for Tier-1 retailers?

The POS integration system was the earlier framework specifically for Tier-1 retailers — connecting their point-of-sale terminals with the FBR. FBR digital invoicing is the broader successor that extends real-time transmission to invoicing systems beyond just retail POS, covering wholesalers, manufacturers, and B2B suppliers in scope.

What does an FBR digital invoicing audit look like?

The FBR runs an automated reconciliation between your transmitted invoices and your monthly sales tax return. If the totals don't match, or if invoices in a series go missing, you receive a query. A field audit is the next step if the desk-based query isn't resolved. This is one reason why getting your bookkeeping right alongside the invoicing matters — the two have to reconcile.

Need Help with FBR Digital Invoicing?

FBR digital invoicing is one of those compliance items where doing it badly costs more than not doing it at all — a misconfigured integration can transmit wrong invoices to the FBR, and undoing those is painful. Getting it right the first time is cheaper.

title: FBR Online Verification — Complete Pakistan Lookup Guide
excerpt: FBR online verification covers NTN, ATL, STRN, and withholding-agent lookups via the official FBR portal. Here's exactly how to use each in under 60 seconds.
content:
What Is FBR Online Verification?

FBR online verification is the umbrella term for the public lookup tools the Federal Board of Revenue offers via its IRIS portal to check a person's or business's standing on Pakistan's tax registers. Anyone — taxpayer, vendor, or counterparty — can use these tools without a login. The current FBR online verification menu covers 13 distinct lookups:

  • Active Taxpayer List (Income Tax) — the main ATL for income-tax filers
  • Active Taxpayer List (AJK) — separate ATL for Azad Jammu & Kashmir
  • Active Taxpayer Lists — Downloads — bulk ATL files
  • Active Taxpayer List (Sales Tax) — sales-tax-specific ATL
  • Taxpayer Profile Inquiry — full registration profile by NTN / CNIC / STRN
  • Blacklisted Taxpayer List (Sales Tax) — flagged sales-tax registrants
  • Exemption Certificate — verify any tax exemption certificate
  • Notices/Orders Verification — confirm an FBR notice is genuine
  • Computerized Payment Receipt (CPR) — verify a tax payment
  • POS Invoice Verification — Tier-1 retailer invoice authenticity
  • Property Certificate Verification (u/s 7E) — capital value tax certificate check
  • Payment Slip ID (PSID) / CPR Verification — confirm a payment reference
  • DNFBP Registration Status — Designated Non-Financial Business or Profession

Each answers a different question, but they all share one portal — and most run in under 60 seconds. This guide walks through the lookups you'll use most often, with direct links and the gotchas you should know.

Why FBR Online Verification Matters

If you run a business in Pakistan, FBR online verification is what stops you from paying double tax. Section after section of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 charges roughly twice the rate on payments to Non-Active-Taxpayer-List (Non-ATL) persons. Before you pay any vendor, contractor, supplier, or service provider a substantial amount, a 30-second FBR verification:

  • Confirms their NTN is real and matches the legal name on the invoice
  • Tells you their current ATL status — so you apply the correct withholding rate
  • Surfaces any discrepancy that should be resolved before the payment, not after

For a deeper dive on why ATL status changes the rates you pay or deduct, see our complete ATL benefits guide.

How to Use FBR Online Verification for an NTN

The most common form of FBR online verification is an NTN lookup. The official tool sits inside the FBR's IRIS portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk.

  1. Open the FBR IRIS portal
  2. Choose your input type: NTN (7 digits) or CNIC (13 digits)
  3. Enter the number without dashes
  4. Solve the captcha
  5. Click Verify
  6. Read the result: registered name, status (active/inactive), and ATL status

For a complete walkthrough — including screenshots, troubleshooting, and the SMS shortcut — see our dedicated NTN verification online guide.

How to Use FBR Online Verification for ATL Status

An ATL check is essentially the second half of the same FBR online verification call — when you verify an NTN, the result already includes ATL status. But there are two FBR-specific shortcuts dedicated to ATL status:

  • SMS to 9966 — text your CNIC or NTN (no dashes); the FBR replies with the registered name and current ATL status within seconds
  • FBR IRIS portal — iris.fbr.gov.pk publishes the latest ATL list with downloadable extracts

The ATL refreshes weekly. (Your underlying NTN doesn't change — only the ATL status against it.) A status of "Inactive" today may flip to "Active" once the next refresh runs after a return is filed. For why this matters across banking, vehicles, and property, see benefits of being on the ATL.

How to Use FBR Online Verification for STRN (Sales Tax)

Businesses registered for sales tax receive a Sales Tax Registration Number (STRN) in addition to an NTN. To verify any STRN online, the FBR's IRIS portal accepts the STRN as the input number. The result confirms whether the business is sales-tax-registered and whether the registration is currently active.

This is essential for input tax adjustments — you can only claim input tax against suppliers who hold a valid STRN at the time of the invoice. Verify before posting any input tax claim.

The Most-Used FBR Online Verification Lookups

Of the 13 lookups available on the FBR portal, three are used almost daily in Pakistani business: NTN / CNIC verification, ATL status, and STRN validity. The rest cover specific compliance edge cases (exemptions, notices, payments, POS invoices, 7E property certificates, etc.) that you'll reach for less frequently — but they're all in the same place when you need them.

Direct Links to Every FBR Online Verification Tool

Common FBR Online Verification Errors and Fixes

"Record not available" or "NTN not found"

Three usual causes: typo in the NTN/CNIC, the person was never registered with FBR, or the record is archived. Re-check the digits — particularly when transcribed from handwriting. If the number is correct and still not found, the person likely needs to register on the IRIS portal.

Registered name doesn't match what you expected

Either the NTN belongs to someone else with a similar CNIC, or the person's legal name on file with FBR differs from their everyday name. Always confirm the legal name with the counterparty before relying on the verification.

Captcha won't load or expires

Try a different browser, clear your cache, or wait a few minutes — the FBR's captcha service occasionally times out. If the website is unresponsive, fall back to the SMS shortcut (9966) for ATL-only checks.

"Inactive" or "Not on ATL" — what now?

The taxpayer hasn't filed a return for the latest tax year. They need to file (deadline is typically 30 September). Once filed, the ATL status — not the NTN — updates with the next weekly refresh. Until they're on the ATL, any payments to them are subject to the higher Non-ATL withholding rates across most sections.

When to Hire a Tax Professional Instead

FBR online verification is straightforward, but the moment you need to act on what the verification tells you — claim withholding tax credits, contest a notice, or correct a registration mismatch — DIY stops being enough. Our Pakistan income tax team handles end-to-end FBR work: NTN registration, ATL maintenance, return filing, withholding tax compliance, and notice handling. Book a free consultation if you'd like us to take it from here.

Frequently Asked Questions About FBR Online Verification

Is FBR online verification free?

Yes. The FBR's online verification portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk and the SMS shortcut to 9966 are both free public services. No login is required.

Can foreigners use FBR online verification?

Yes. The verification portal is open to anyone worldwide — no Pakistani identity is needed to perform a lookup. Overseas Pakistanis routinely verify their own ATL status this way before sending remittances or buying property.

How often does the FBR ATL update?

The first ATL of each tax year is published on 1 March. The list refreshes weekly after that, with newly compliant taxpayers added throughout the year as they file returns and pay any applicable surcharge. (The NTN itself does not update weekly — only the ATL status against it.)

Can I verify a company's NTN using its STRN?

Yes. The FBR online verification portal accepts NTN, CNIC, or STRN as input. The result includes the income tax and sales tax registrations linked to the entity.

What's the difference between NTN verification and FBR online verification?

NTN verification is one type of FBR online verification — specifically, the income tax registration check. The broader term covers ATL, STRN, and any other public lookup the FBR offers via its portal.

Does FBR online verification work for deceased taxpayers?

The portal still returns historical information but flags the status appropriately. Estate-tax filings are handled separately; consult a tax professional if you're managing a deceased taxpayer's affairs.

The Bottom Line on FBR Online Verification

FBR online verification is the cheapest insurance available to anyone transacting in Pakistan's tax system. A 60-second lookup before paying any sizeable invoice protects you from paying double withholding tax, posting a bad input tax claim, or accepting a fake NTN. Bookmark the IRIS portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk and the 9966 SMS shortcut — and verify your own status at least twice a year, especially before any large transaction.

title: NTN Verification Online — How to Check FBR ATL Status
excerpt: How to verify any NTN online via the FBR portal in under 60 seconds — step-by-step ATL status check, CNIC lookup, and what to do if not listed.
content:
What Is NTN Verification Online and Why Does It Matter?

If you're hiring a contractor in Pakistan, paying a vendor, or about to make any large transaction with another business, an NTN verification online check takes under 60 seconds and tells you exactly who you're dealing with — and whether they're on the FBR's Active Taxpayer List (ATL).

An NTN (National Tax Number) is the FBR's unique tax identifier for individuals and businesses. Verifying an NTN online confirms:

  • The number is real and matches the legal name attached to it
  • The taxpayer's current status — active or inactive
  • Whether they're on the latest ATL (which determines withholding tax rates on banking, vehicle, and property transactions)
  • Their registered tax circle and Regional Tax Office

For your own NTN, online verification is how you confirm your ATL status before each year's transactions. Being on the ATL saves up to 50% on withholding tax across most major financial flows.

How to Verify Any NTN Online via the FBR Portal

The FBR provides public verification tools that are free and require no login.

  2. Choose your parameter type: NTN or CNIC
  3. For NTN: enter the 7-digit number. For CNIC: enter the 13-digit number without dashes
  4. Solve the captcha shown on screen
  5. Click Verify
  6. The portal shows: registered name, status (active/inactive), and current ATL status

Understanding Your NTN Verification Result

The portal returns three pieces of information you should always check:

  • Registered name — must exactly match the person or company you expected. A mismatch means either a typo in the NTN/CNIC you entered, or the legal entity is different from what you assumed.
  • Status (Active / Inactive) — Inactive means the person hasn't filed a recent return. Doing business with an inactive taxpayer means higher withholding deductions for you.
  • ATL status — Indicates whether the taxpayer is on the latest published Active Taxpayer List. The list refreshes every March based on returns filed for the previous tax year.

Why ATL Status Is the Most Important Outcome of NTN Verification

The FBR uses ATL status to apply differential withholding rates. Being on the ATL typically saves 50% or more on:

  • Banking transaction withholding tax
  • Vehicle registration and transfer tax
  • Property purchase and sale tax
  • Cash withdrawal withholding
  • Imports, exports, and dividend withholding

If your verification shows "Inactive" or "Not on ATL," your next year's transactions will be more expensive than they need to be. Read our complete guide on ATL benefits for the full breakdown.

NTN Verification by SMS — The Quick Method

If you don't want to use the FBR website, the same verification is available via SMS:

  1. Open your messaging app and create a new SMS to 9966
  2. Send your 13-digit CNIC (or 7-digit NTN) without dashes
  3. Within seconds, you receive a reply showing the registered name and current ATL status

This works on any Pakistani mobile network and doesn't require internet access. Useful when you're on the go and need a quick ATL check before paying a vendor.

Common NTN Verification Problems and How to Fix Them

"NTN not found" or "Record not available"

Three usual causes: the NTN was typed incorrectly, the person was never registered with FBR, or their record was archived. Re-enter carefully — if still not found, the person likely doesn't have an NTN and needs to register.

The registered name doesn't match what I expected

The NTN may belong to someone else with a similar CNIC, or the person's legal name on file with FBR differs from what they go by. Always confirm the legal name with the taxpayer before relying on the verification.

Captcha won't load

Try a different browser, clear your cache, or wait a few minutes — FBR's captcha service occasionally times out. If the website is down entirely, use the SMS method to 9966 as a fallback.

The portal shows me as "Inactive" — what now?

You probably haven't filed a return for the latest tax year. File your return (the deadline is typically 30 September). After filing, your ATL status updates with the next ATL refresh in March. See our complete filing guide for Pakistan 2026.

How to Register for an NTN If You Don't Have One

If verification shows you don't have an NTN, register through the FBR's IRIS portal:

  1. Visit iris.fbr.gov.pk
  2. Click "Registration for Unregistered Person"
  3. Provide CNIC, contact details, address, and source of income
  4. Submit and receive your NTN, typically within 24 hours

Documents you'll need: CNIC scan, a utility bill (proof of address), and bank account details. For business registration, add company incorporation documents and SECP registration number.

Frequently Asked Questions About NTN Verification Online

Is NTN verification online free?

Yes. The FBR's online verification portal and the SMS service to 9966 are both free public services. No login or registration is required.

Can I verify someone's NTN online using only their CNIC?

Yes. Both the FBR portal and the SMS service accept either NTN (7 digits) or CNIC (13 digits) as input.

What's the difference between NTN and STRN?

NTN is your tax identification number for income tax. STRN (Sales Tax Registration Number) is separate and applies only if you're registered for sales tax. Some businesses have both.

Can a foreigner verify an NTN online?

Yes — the verification portal is open to anyone. No Pakistani identity is required to perform a lookup. Overseas Pakistanis routinely verify their own ATL status this way.

The Bottom Line

title: FBR Powers to Enforce Filing — Non-Filer Guide Pakistan
excerpt: FBR can now disable your mobile phone, cut your electricity, and restrict your travel if you don't file. Here's what Section 114B means for non-filers in Pakistan.
content:
The Scale of the Problem

In 2023, Pakistan had approximately 11.4 million registered taxpayers — but only around 5.3 million actually filed their income tax returns. That's less than 50% compliance among registered taxpayers. The real gap is even wider when you include millions of people who should be registered but aren't.

FBR has been struggling with this compliance gap for years, and traditional measures haven't worked.

What FBR Has Tried So Far

Higher Withholding Tax for Non-Filers

The most significant measure has been doubling withholding tax rates for non-filers. In most transaction categories — banking, property, vehicles, dividends — non-filers pay twice the rate that filers pay.

While this creates a financial incentive to file, it hasn't been enough. Many non-filers simply absorb the higher cost rather than entering the tax system.

Section 114B — FBR's New Powers

Through the Finance Act 2022, FBR introduced Section 114B in the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. This gives FBR unprecedented enforcement powers against non-filers:

1. Disable Mobile Phones and SIMs

FBR can direct telecom operators to deactivate mobile connections of non-filers. In a country where mobile connectivity is essential for business and daily life, this is a powerful pressure tool.

2. Disconnect Electricity

FBR can instruct electricity distribution companies to discontinue electricity connections to the premises of non-filers.

3. Disconnect Gas Supply

Similarly, gas connections can be discontinued for individuals and businesses that fail to file their returns.

4. Restrict Foreign Travel

FBR can place non-filers on the Exit Control List (ECL) or restrict their ability to travel internationally until returns are filed.

Will These Powers Work?

These are the most aggressive enforcement tools FBR has ever been given. Whether they will meaningfully improve compliance is still being debated. The practical implementation — identifying non-filers, coordinating with telecom companies and utilities — is complex. But the message is clear: the cost of not filing is going up significantly.

title: Banking Withholding Tax Pakistan — Filer vs Non-Filer Rates

content:
What Is Withholding Tax on Banking Transactions?

Withholding tax on bank transactions is a tax deducted at source by banks on certain financial activities — most notably cash withdrawals. The policy is designed to promote tax return filing by making banking significantly more expensive for non-filers.

Understanding Filers, Non-Filers, and Late Filers

In Pakistan, taxpayers fall into three categories:

  • Filers: Individuals or businesses that have filed their latest income tax return on time and appear on the Active Taxpayer List (ATL)
  • Late Filers: Those who filed after the due date — they may appear on ATL but with a delay
  • Non-Filers: Those who have not filed their latest return — they face the highest withholding rates

This distinction is crucial because it directly determines how much tax your bank deducts from every transaction.

Withholding Tax Rates for Tax Year 2025

Non-Filers

Withholding tax on cash withdrawals is 0.6% where the total amount exceeds Rs. 50,000 in aggregate in a single day. This applies to every withdrawal above the threshold — and it adds up fast.

Filers and Late Filers

There is no withholding tax on cash withdrawals for filers and late filers for tax year 2025. This is a massive financial benefit of being on the ATL.

Can You Claim This Tax Back?

Yes. The withholding tax deducted on cash withdrawals is fully claimable. You can adjust it against your income tax liability or claim a refund when filing your Income Tax Return for the relevant year.

How to Get Your Bank WHT Certificate

You'll need the withholding tax certificate from your bank to claim the tax back. There are several ways to obtain it:

1. Visit Your Bank Branch

Go to the nearest branch where your account is operational and request the certificate directly. Banks are legally bound to provide it.

2. Through Online Banking

Most banks have streamlined this process. Log in to your online banking portal and request the certificate — usually found under "Tax" or "Certificates" section.

3. Through Mobile App

Download your bank's mobile app, log in, and request the certificate. Most major banks (HBL, UBL, MCB, Meezan, etc.) offer this feature.

4. Through Bank Helpline

Call your bank's helpline. After identity verification, they'll email the certificate to your registered email address.

The Bottom Line

If you're a non-filer, you're paying 0.6% on every significant cash withdrawal — money that filers don't pay at all. Over a year, this can cost you hundreds of thousands of rupees. The solution is simple: file your return and get on the ATL. Contact us to get started.

title: Telenor Tax Certificate Download Online (2026 Guide)

content:

The Telenor tax certificate is the official document that proves how much was deducted, and without it you cannot claim the adjustment in your annual income tax return.

What Is a Telenor Tax Certificate?

A Telenor tax certificate (officially the Withholding Tax Statement) is the document Telenor Pakistan issues to confirm how much advance income tax it collected from your mobile or internet usage during a chosen period.

This tax is deducted under Section 236 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. Every recharge, bill, or top-up has a percentage withheld as advance tax and remitted to the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) on your behalf. The certificate consolidates those daily deductions into a single statement.

The key point: this is an adjustable advance tax, not a final tax. Every rupee shown on your Telenor tax certificate can be claimed against your annual income tax liability, which reduces the tax you owe or increases your refund.

Why You Need a Telenor Tax Certificate

Most mobile users pay this tax all year without ever claiming it back. The certificate matters because:

  • You can claim a tax adjustment in your FBR return. The amount on the certificate is entered against your tax liability in IRIS. No certificate, no claim.
  • It increases your refund. When your total withholding exceeds your actual liability, the excess is refundable — but only if it is documented.
  • It serves as proof for employers and auditors. Salaried filers are sometimes asked to provide withholding evidence; this certificate is the accepted record.

Method 1 — Download Your Telenor Tax Certificate via the My Telenor App

This is the fastest method and the one Telenor actively maintains.

  1. Download My Telenor from Google Play (Android) or the App Store (iPhone).
  2. Register with your Telenor mobile number and log in.
  3. Tap the menu icon (three horizontal lines) at the top right of the home screen.
  4. Select Tax Certificate from the menu.
  5. Enter your CNIC, the tax year you need (July to June), and the email address where the PDF should be delivered.
  6. Tap Proceed. A verification code (OTP) is sent to your Telenor number.
  7. Enter the OTP and tap Download.

The certificate appears on screen and a copy lands in your inbox within minutes. Save the PDF; you'll need it during return filing.

Method 2 — Get Your Telenor Tax Certificate via Website Chat

If you don't have the app, the website chat is the next-fastest route.

  1. Visit telenor.com.pk.
  2. Click Help & Support at the top right corner.
  3. Click Telenor Customer Care at the bottom right of the page.
  4. Fill out the form with your name and Telenor mobile number.
  5. In the live chat, request your tax certificate for the desired tax year. Have your CNIC ready — the agent will ask.

The agent emails the PDF directly. Typical response time is 5 to 15 minutes during business hours.

Method 3 — Phone the Telenor Helpline

Telenor's helpline can issue the certificate over a single call.

  • From your Telenor number: dial 345
  • From any other number: dial 042-111-345-100

Follow the voice prompts, provide your CNIC and the tax year you need, and request the certificate be emailed to you. The PDF arrives shortly after the call ends.

Method 4 — Request Your Telenor Tax Certificate by Email

If you prefer written communication, send an email to telenor345@telenor.com.pk with:

  • Scanned CNIC (both sides, PDF preferred)
  • Your Telenor mobile number
  • The tax year you need (for example, 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025 for Tax Year 2025)
  • The email address where the PDF should be sent

Use a clear subject line such as “Request for Telenor Tax Certificate – Tax Year 2025”. Typical turnaround is one to two working days.

Method 5 — Visit a Telenor Franchise

If none of the digital methods work, walk into any Telenor franchise with your CNIC. Staff issue the certificate on the spot. Useful if your mobile number is not registered against your own CNIC and you need to verify ownership in person.

Which Tax-Year Dates Should You Select?

The certificate period must match the Pakistan tax year, which runs July to June — not the calendar year.

Tax YearPeriod to Select
Tax Year 20261 July 2025 – 30 June 2026
Tax Year 20251 July 2024 – 30 June 2025
Tax Year 20241 July 2023 – 30 June 2024

When you file your return for Tax Year 2025, for example, you select the July 2024 to June 2025 range — not January to December.

How Much Tax Does Telenor Deduct?

Mobile services in Pakistan attract advance income tax under Section 236 at a higher rate than landline or broadband. The exact percentage is set by the Finance Act and is revised annually. The deduction applies uniformly to all subscribers; non-filers cannot claim it back, while filers can.

You don't need to calculate this yourself — the certificate states the exact rupee amount deducted, and that's the figure you enter in IRIS. For current rates across all withholding sections, see our Pakistan withholding tax rates lookup.

How to Claim Your Telenor Tax Certificate in Your FBR Return

  1. Download your certificate for the correct tax year.
  2. Log in to FBR IRIS and open your income tax return.
  3. Under Adjustable Tax, locate the entry for telephone/internet bills under Section 236.
  4. Enter the total tax shown on your Telenor certificate.
  5. The amount is automatically adjusted against your liability — reducing tax payable or adding to your refund.

Keep the PDF on file in case FBR requests supporting evidence. While you're in IRIS, check your filer status using our free Bulk ATL Checker — staying on the Active Taxpayer List keeps your future Telenor (and other) withholding rates at the filer level.

Telenor Tax Certificate: Common Problems & Quick Fixes

  • Wrong information on the certificate? Contact Telenor customer care via 345 and request a revised version with correct details.
  • Didn't receive the email? Check your spam or junk folder first, then resubmit the request through a different channel.
  • App not working? Update the My Telenor app, clear cache, or use the website chat or email method instead.
  • SIM not registered against your CNIC? Visit a franchise with the actual SIM owner's CNIC. Telenor cannot issue a certificate to a name that doesn't match the SIM record.
  • Need a certificate for multiple years? Request them separately — one certificate per tax year is the standard format.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Telenor tax certificate free?

Yes. All five methods — app, web chat, phone, email, and franchise — are free of charge.

Can I get a Telenor tax certificate for previous years?

Yes. Telenor maintains historic records and can issue certificates for past tax years. Just specify the tax year (July to June) when requesting.

Yes. The tax is collected from every Telenor subscriber. But only filers can claim it back in their return, which is one more reason to file. Verify your filer status using our ATL Checker.

It is adjustable advance tax under Section 236. The full amount shown on your Telenor tax certificate can be claimed against your annual income tax liability in your FBR return.

What information is on a Telenor tax certificate?

The certificate shows your CNIC, registered name, Telenor mobile number, tax year covered, monthly breakdown of recharges, total tax deducted, and the section of the Income Tax Ordinance under which it was collected.

Do I need a separate certificate for each Telenor SIM I own?

Yes. Each Telenor mobile number generates its own withholding tax statement. If you have multiple Telenor SIMs registered against your CNIC, request a certificate for each number and total them when claiming.

What is the difference between a Telenor bill and a Telenor tax certificate?

A monthly bill or recharge receipt shows the amount you paid. The Telenor tax certificate shows the withholding tax deducted over a chosen period. Only the certificate is valid evidence for an FBR claim.

Mobile withholding deductions are small per recharge. Across a year, and combined with your PTCL, banking, and other deductions, they add up to real money you can recover.

The certificate shows your CNIC, registered name, Jazz mobile number, tax year covered, monthly breakdown of recharges or bills, total tax deducted, and the section of the Income Tax Ordinance under which it was collected.

Do I need a separate certificate for each Jazz SIM I own?

Yes. Each Jazz mobile number generates its own withholding tax statement. If you have multiple Jazz, Warid, or Mobilink SIMs registered against your CNIC, request a certificate for each number and total them when claiming.

Is the SIMOSA app the same as Jazz World?

SIMOSA is the rebranded version of the Jazz World app. If you still have Jazz World installed, the tax certificate flow works the same way; if you reinstall, you'll get SIMOSA from the app stores.

What is the difference between a Jazz bill and a Jazz tax certificate?

A monthly bill or recharge receipt shows the amount you paid. The Jazz tax certificate shows the withholding tax deducted over a chosen period. Only the certificate is valid evidence for an FBR claim.

Don't Leave Claimable Tax on the Table

Mobile withholding deductions are small per recharge. Across a year, and combined with your PTCL, Telenor, banking, and other deductions, they add up to real money you can recover.

title: PTCL Tax Certificate Download Online (2026 Guide)
excerpt: Download your PTCL tax certificate online in minutes via the PTCL website or WhatsApp, and learn how to claim the deducted tax in your FBR return.
heroImageAlt: PTCL tax certificate online portal — Withholding Tax Statement inquiry form with service type, area code, phone number, and Account ID fields
content:
Quick answer: Download your PTCL tax certificate at ptcl.com.pk/CustomerTax/TaxInquiry in under two minutes — or message PTCL WhatsApp at 0331 218 1218. You'll need your area code, phone number, and the Account ID printed on your bill. The certificate shows the withholding tax deducted from your landline, broadband, or EVO/Charji bills under Section 236, which you claim in your FBR return to reduce your tax bill.

If you pay PTCL for a landline, broadband, or EVO/Charji connection, PTCL has been deducting advance income tax from every bill. That money isn't gone — it is recoverable. The PTCL tax certificate is the document that proves how much was deducted, and without it you cannot claim the adjustment in your annual return.

What Is a PTCL Tax Certificate?

A PTCL tax certificate (officially the Withholding Tax Statement) is an official document from Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited. It shows the total advance income tax collected from your bills over a chosen period.

This tax is deducted under Section 236 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001. The law requires telephone and internet providers to collect advance tax from subscribers. It applies to:

  • Landline telephone connections
  • Broadband internet
  • EVO / Charji wireless devices

The key point: this is an adjustable advance tax, not a final tax. Every rupee shown on your certificate can be claimed against your annual income tax liability, which reduces the tax you owe or increases your refund.

Why You Need a PTCL Tax Certificate

Most people pay this tax all year without ever claiming it back. The certificate matters because:

  • You can claim a tax adjustment in your FBR return. The amount on the certificate is entered against your tax liability in IRIS. No certificate, no claim.
  • It increases your refund. When your total withholding exceeds your actual liability, the excess is refundable — but only if it is documented.
  • It serves as proof for employers and auditors. Salaried filers are sometimes asked to provide withholding evidence; this certificate is the accepted record.

Method 1 — Download Your PTCL Tax Certificate from the Website

This is the most reliable method and works for every service type.

  1. Go to ptcl.com.pk/CustomerTax/TaxInquiry.
  2. Select your Service Type — Landline, Broadband, or EVO/Charji.
  3. Choose your Area Code from the dropdown.
  4. Enter your Phone Number (without the area code).
  5. Enter your Account ID — printed on the front of your PTCL bill.
  6. Select the date range for the certificate — July to June of the relevant tax year (see the table below).
  7. Type the Captcha characters shown.
  8. Click “Inquire Tax”.

Your certificate appears on screen with the total tax deducted, ready to save or print as a PDF.

Tip: The portal works in any mobile browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), so you don't need a desktop. PTCL does not currently offer this through its mobile app.

Method 2 — Get Your PTCL Tax Certificate on WhatsApp

If you don't have your Account ID handy, WhatsApp is the fastest route:

  1. Save and message 0331 218 1218 — send “Hi” to start
  2. From the automated menu, select “Tax Certificate”
  3. Choose the period you need
  4. PTCL sends the certificate as a PDF, directly in the chat

This works when your mobile number is registered with your PTCL account. If it isn't — or you hit an error — use the website method above.

Which Tax-Year Dates Should You Select?

This is where most people get stuck. For an income tax return, the certificate period must match the tax year, which runs July to June, not the calendar year.

Tax YearPeriod to Select
Tax Year 20261 July 2025 – 30 June 2026
Tax Year 20251 July 2024 – 30 June 2025
Tax Year 20241 July 2023 – 30 June 2024

When you file your return for Tax Year 2025, for example, you select the July 2024 to June 2025 range — not January to December.

PTCL Bill vs PTCL Tax Certificate — Don't Confuse Them

These are two different documents, and only one is valid for your return:

DocumentShowsUse
PTCL BillMonthly charges and usagePaying your bill
PTCL Tax CertificateTotal withholding tax deducted over a periodClaiming the adjustment in your FBR return

A monthly bill is not acceptable evidence for a tax claim. You need the consolidated withholding tax certificate for the full tax year.

How Much Tax Does PTCL Deduct?

Advance tax on telephone and internet services is collected under Section 236. For landline subscribers, the long-standing rate is 10% on the portion of the bill exceeding Rs. 1,000, while internet and mobile services are charged at a higher rate.

One thing worth getting right — and where many online guides are wrong: this telephone and internet withholding is collected uniformly from all subscribers. Unlike property (236K), vehicle, or several other advance taxes, it is not split into separate “filer” and “non-filer” rates. Everyone pays the same; the difference is that filers can claim it back, while non-filers simply lose it.

You don't actually need to calculate any of this — the certificate states the exact rupee amount deducted, and that's the figure you claim. For other withholding tax sections affecting your business or personal transactions, see our Pakistan withholding tax rates lookup.

How to Claim Your PTCL Tax Certificate in Your FBR Return

  1. Download your certificate for the correct tax year (July–June).
  2. Log in to FBR IRIS and open your income tax return.
  3. Under Adjustable Tax, locate the entry for telephone/internet bills under Section 236.
  4. Enter the total tax shown on your PTCL certificate.
  5. The amount is automatically adjusted against your liability — reducing tax payable or adding to your refund.

Keep the PDF certificate on file in case FBR requests supporting evidence. While you're in IRIS, verify your filer status using our free Bulk ATL Checker — staying on the Active Taxpayer List ensures lower withholding rates across all your other transactions.

PTCL Tax Certificate: Common Problems & Quick Fixes

  • “No record found”: Check that your Account ID exactly matches the bill, and that you've picked the correct service type (Landline vs Broadband vs EVO/Charji are separate).
  • Wrong amount showing: Confirm the date range covers the full July–June tax year, not the calendar year.
  • WhatsApp not responding: Your mobile number may not be linked to the PTCL account — use the website method instead.
  • Captcha keeps failing: Refresh the page for a new code; the characters are case-sensitive.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the PTCL tax certificate free?

Yes. Downloading it from the PTCL website or via WhatsApp is completely free.

Can I get a PTCL tax certificate for previous years?

Yes. Select the relevant July–June date range on the portal to pull a PTCL tax certificate for an earlier tax year. PTCL retains records for several past tax years.

Do non-filers pay PTCL withholding tax?

Yes. The tax is collected from everyone. But only filers can claim it back in their return, which is one more reason to file. Verify your filer status with our ATL Checker.

Is PTCL withholding tax adjustable or final?

It is adjustable advance tax under Section 236. The full amount shown on your PTCL tax certificate can be claimed against your annual income tax liability in your FBR return.

What is the difference between a PTCL bill and a PTCL tax certificate?

The bill shows monthly charges. The PTCL tax certificate shows the total withholding tax deducted over a chosen period. Only the certificate is valid evidence for an FBR claim.

Don't Leave Claimable Tax on the Table

The withholding tax PTCL deducts is small each month. Across a year, and combined with your mobile, banking, and other deductions, it adds up to real money you can recover.

title: Tax on Foreign Income in Pakistan — Overseas Filer Guide
excerpt: Do overseas Pakistanis need to pay tax in Pakistan? What about foreign remittances, property income abroad, and dual tax treaties? Complete guide.
content:
Do Overseas Pakistanis Need to Pay Tax in Pakistan?

It depends on your tax residency status. If you are a tax resident of Pakistan, you are taxable on your worldwide income — including foreign salary, business income, rental income, and investment returns earned outside Pakistan. If you are a non-resident, you are only taxable on Pakistan-source income.

This distinction is the single most important factor in determining your tax obligations. Many overseas Pakistanis assume they have no tax liability back home, but this assumption can be costly if they still qualify as tax residents.

Resident vs Non-Resident: How Is It Determined?

Under Section 82 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, you are considered a tax resident of Pakistan if:

  • You are present in Pakistan for 183 days or more in a tax year (July 1 to June 30), OR
  • You are an employee of the federal or provincial government posted abroad, OR
  • You are a Pakistani citizen who is not a tax resident of any other country

The third condition is often overlooked. If you are living abroad but have not obtained tax residency in another country (for example, you are on a temporary visa and not filing taxes locally), Pakistan may consider you a tax resident by default.

A non-resident is anyone who does not meet any of the above conditions. Non-residents are only taxed on income that originates from Pakistan — such as rental income from Pakistani property, dividends from Pakistani companies, or business income from a permanent establishment in Pakistan.

Tax Treatment of Foreign Remittances

One of the most common questions from overseas Pakistanis is: "Will I be taxed on money I send back to Pakistan?"

The short answer is generally no, provided the remittance comes from a legitimate foreign source. Under Section 111(4) of the Income Tax Ordinance, any amount received through normal banking channels from outside Pakistan is exempt from tax, and the FBR cannot question its source.

This protection applies to:

  • Salary remittances from overseas employment
  • Business income earned abroad and remitted to Pakistan
  • Gift money sent from abroad
  • Savings and investment returns transferred to Pakistani bank accounts

The key requirement is that the funds must enter Pakistan through formal banking channels (bank transfers, telegraphic transfers, or home remittance schemes). Cash carried physically or sent through informal channels (hundi/hawala) does not receive this protection.

Foreign Property Income

If you are a tax resident of Pakistan and own property abroad that generates rental income, that income is taxable in Pakistan. You must report it in your annual tax return and pay tax at the applicable slab rates.

However, if you have already paid tax on the same income in the country where the property is located, you may be eligible for a foreign tax credit under Pakistan's Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs) to avoid being taxed twice on the same income.

Double Taxation Agreements

Pakistan has signed Double Taxation Agreements (DTAs) with over 65 countries, including the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the UK, the USA, Canada, Australia, and most European nations. These agreements determine:

  • Which country has the primary right to tax specific types of income
  • Maximum withholding tax rates on cross-border payments (dividends, interest, royalties)
  • Methods to eliminate double taxation (credit method or exemption method)

Under most DTAs, if you have paid tax on income in the foreign country, Pakistan will either exempt that income or give you a credit for the foreign tax paid against your Pakistani tax liability.

Section 7E — Deemed Income on Assets

Under Section 7E of the Income Tax Ordinance, a deemed income of 5% of the fair market value of certain capital assets is taxed at 20%. This effectively creates a 1% annual tax on the value of immovable property held in Pakistan.

This applies to both residents and non-residents who own immovable property in Pakistan. Exemptions exist for:

  • One self-occupied property (up to a specified area)
  • Property allotted to government employees under government schemes
  • Agricultural land (subject to conditions)
  • Property held by certain categories of overseas Pakistanis (specific exemptions have been introduced and modified over successive Finance Acts)

This section is controversial and has been challenged in courts. We recommend consulting with a tax advisor to determine the current applicability to your specific situation.

NTN Requirements for Overseas Pakistanis

If you own property in Pakistan, have bank accounts generating taxable income, or earn any Pakistan-source income, you need a National Tax Number (NTN) and should file annual tax returns. Being on the FBR's Active Taxpayer List (ATL) provides significant benefits:

  • Lower withholding tax rates on property transactions, banking, and investments
  • Reduced tax on property purchases and sales
  • Easier documentation when buying or selling property in Pakistan

Overseas Pakistanis can register for an NTN and file returns through the FBR IRIS portal online, without needing to visit Pakistan.

Practical Steps for Overseas Pakistanis

  1. Determine your tax residency status — check if you meet the 183-day rule or any other residency test
  2. Always remit through banking channels — this protects your funds under Section 111(4)
  3. Register for NTN if you own assets in Pakistan or earn Pakistan-source income
  4. File annual returns to stay on the Active Taxpayer List and benefit from lower withholding rates
  5. Claim foreign tax credits where applicable under DTAs
  6. Keep records of all foreign income, taxes paid abroad, and remittances

Need Professional Guidance?

Tax obligations for overseas Pakistanis can be complex, especially when multiple jurisdictions are involved. Our income tax specialists work with overseas Pakistanis across the Gulf, Europe, and North America to ensure compliance in Pakistan while minimizing double taxation. Contact us for a consultation.

title: Pakistan Income Tax Slabs 2026-27 — Salaried & Business
excerpt: Income tax slabs for tax year 2026-27 in Pakistan under the Finance Act 2026. New 8-bracket salaried table, business and AOP rates, and worked examples.
content:
Income Tax Slabs for Tax Year 2026-27

Pakistan's income tax rates for individuals are set by the Finance Act and depend on whether you are a salaried individual, a non-salaried individual (business person), or an Association of Persons (AOP). Tax year 2026-27 — formally Tax Year 2027 — runs from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

The Finance Act 2026 received presidential assent on 25 June 2026 and took effect on 1 July 2026. It delivered the largest restructuring of the salaried slabs in several years: eight brackets instead of six, lower rates in the middle, and the withdrawal of the 9% surcharge. Business and AOP rates were left unchanged.

Below are the complete tables with worked examples so you can check your own liability.

Salaried Individuals — Tax Slabs 2026-27

These rates apply to individuals whose salary income is more than 75% of their total income:

  • Up to PKR 600,000 — 0% (no tax)
  • PKR 600,001 to PKR 1,200,000 — 1% of the amount exceeding PKR 600,000
  • PKR 1,200,001 to PKR 2,200,000 — PKR 6,000 + 11% of the amount exceeding PKR 1,200,000
  • PKR 2,200,001 to PKR 3,200,000 — PKR 116,000 + 20% of the amount exceeding PKR 2,200,000
  • PKR 3,200,001 to PKR 4,100,000 — PKR 316,000 + 25% of the amount exceeding PKR 3,200,000
  • PKR 4,100,001 to PKR 5,600,000 — PKR 541,000 + 29% of the amount exceeding PKR 4,100,000
  • PKR 5,600,001 to PKR 7,000,000 — PKR 976,000 + 32% of the amount exceeding PKR 5,600,000
  • Above PKR 7,000,000 — PKR 1,424,000 + 35% of the amount exceeding PKR 7,000,000

What Changed From 2025-26

Four changes matter, and together they cut the bill for almost every salaried taxpayer:

  • The 23% bracket was cut to 20% (PKR 2.2m–3.2m).
  • The 30% bracket was cut to 25% (PKR 3.2m–4.1m).
  • The top 35% rate now starts at PKR 7 million instead of PKR 4.1 million, with two new intermediate brackets at 29% and 32% filling the gap.
  • The 9% surcharge under section 4AB on taxable income above PKR 10 million was withdrawn for salaried individuals. The top effective marginal rate therefore falls from 38.15% to 35%.

Calculation Example — Salaried Individual

Suppose your annual taxable salary is PKR 2,500,000:

  1. First PKR 600,000 — tax: PKR 0
  2. Next PKR 600,000 (600,001 to 1,200,000) — tax: 1% x 600,000 = PKR 6,000
  3. Next PKR 1,000,000 (1,200,001 to 2,200,000) — tax: 11% x 1,000,000 = PKR 110,000
  4. Remaining PKR 300,000 (2,200,001 to 2,500,000) — tax: 20% x 300,000 = PKR 60,000

Total tax: PKR 176,000 — an effective rate of 7.0%.

On the 2025-26 slabs the same salary attracted PKR 255,000, so this taxpayer is PKR 79,000 a year better off. You can run your own figure — and compare any two tax years side by side — with our Pakistan salary tax calculator.

Non-Salaried Individuals (Business) — Tax Slabs 2026-27

These rates apply to individuals whose salary income is 75% or less of their total income — business owners, self-employed professionals, and freelancers. The Finance Act 2026 left these brackets unchanged, so the 2026-27 rates are identical to 2025-26:

  • Up to PKR 600,000 — 0%
  • PKR 600,001 to PKR 1,200,000 — 15% of the amount exceeding PKR 600,000
  • PKR 1,200,001 to PKR 1,600,000 — PKR 90,000 + 20% of the amount exceeding PKR 1,200,000
  • PKR 1,600,001 to PKR 3,200,000 — PKR 170,000 + 30% of the amount exceeding PKR 1,600,000
  • PKR 3,200,001 to PKR 5,600,000 — PKR 650,000 + 40% of the amount exceeding PKR 3,200,000
  • PKR 5,600,001 and above — PKR 1,610,000 + 45% of the amount exceeding PKR 5,600,000

Non-salaried individuals face materially higher rates at every bracket than salaried persons — a deliberate policy to encourage formal employment and documentation of business income. That gap widened in 2026-27, because the salaried slabs were cut while the business slabs were not.

A 10% surcharge under section 4AB still applies to non-salaried individuals and AOPs whose taxable income exceeds PKR 10 million. This is the surcharge that was withdrawn for salaried taxpayers — it remains in force for business income.

Calculation Example — Business Individual

Suppose your annual business income is PKR 2,000,000:

  1. First PKR 600,000 — tax: PKR 0
  2. Next PKR 600,000 (600,001 to 1,200,000) — tax: 15% x 600,000 = PKR 90,000
  3. Remaining PKR 800,000 (1,200,001 to 2,000,000) — tax: 20% x 400,000 + 30% x 400,000 = PKR 200,000

Total tax: PKR 290,000 (effective rate: 14.5%)

Association of Persons (AOPs)

AOPs (partnerships, joint ventures, and unincorporated entities) are taxed at the same rates as non-salaried individuals. However, there are important differences:

  • The AOP itself is the taxable entity — not the individual partners
  • Profit distribution to partners is not separately taxed (to avoid double taxation)
  • If the AOP fails to file a return, each partner may be individually assessed on their share of the AOP income at their applicable individual rates
  • An AOP that is a professional firm prohibited from incorporating by law or by the rules of its regulating body (for example, firms of chartered accountants or advocates) is capped at a maximum rate of 40% rather than 45%

Companies — Corporate Tax Rate

This article covers individual and AOP slabs. Corporate rates are summarised below for orientation only — confirm the current year's position against the FBR income tax rate schedules before relying on them:

  • Public companies listed on the stock exchange: 29%
  • Private companies (not listed): 29%
  • Banking companies: 39%
  • Small companies (turnover up to PKR 250 million): 20%

Super Tax and the Section 4AB Surcharge — Not the Same Thing

These two charges are routinely confused, including in a lot of published guidance. They are separate:

  • Section 4AB surcharge — a surcharge on the tax payable where taxable income exceeds PKR 10 million. For 2026-27 it is 10% for non-salaried individuals and AOPs, and has been withdrawn entirely for salaried individuals.
  • Section 4C super tax — a separate levy on high earning persons, applying at tiered rates from 1% to 10% and only biting at much higher income levels (PKR 150 million and above under the current tiers). Sector-specific rates apply to banking, beverages, cement, and other specified sectors.

If you earn PKR 12 million from a business, you are in scope for the section 4AB surcharge — not for super tax. Confusing the two is one of the most common sources of over-provisioning we see in client accounts.

Minimum Tax

Under Section 113, a minimum tax of 1.25% of turnover applies where the tax calculated on taxable income is less than 1.25% of the person's gross turnover. This ensures that even businesses showing losses or minimal profits contribute some tax revenue.

How to Calculate Your Tax

Follow these steps:

  1. Determine your total income from all sources (salary, business, property, capital gains, other)
  2. Claim allowable deductions (zakat, donations to approved institutions, pension fund contributions)
  3. Calculate taxable income (total income minus deductions)
  4. Apply the relevant slab based on whether you are salaried or non-salaried
  5. Subtract tax credits (if applicable) and adjustable withholding taxes
  6. Pay the balance or claim a refund

For a quick estimate, use our Pakistan salary tax calculator — it now carries the 2026-27 slabs alongside every year back to 2022 — or contact us for a precise calculation.

title: How to Pay Income Tax in Pakistan — IRIS, Bank, Online
excerpt: Step-by-step guide to paying income tax in Pakistan through the FBR IRIS portal, bank challans, online banking, and ATMs.
content:
How to Pay Income Tax in Pakistan

Income tax in Pakistan can be paid through the FBR IRIS portal, online banking, over-the-counter at bank branches, or through ATMs. The process starts with generating a Payment Slip ID (PSID) on the IRIS portal, which you then use to make the payment through your preferred method.

This guide walks you through each payment method step by step, covers important deadlines, and highlights common mistakes that can delay your payment processing.

Step 1: Generate a PSID on the IRIS Portal

Regardless of which payment method you choose, the first step is always to generate a PSID (Payment Slip ID) through the FBR's IRIS portal. The PSID is a unique 17-digit number that links your payment to your tax account.

  1. Visit the IRIS portal at iris.fbr.gov.pk
  2. Log in with your NTN/CNIC and password
  3. Navigate to "Payments" from the main menu
  4. Select "Create Payment"
  5. Choose the payment type (e.g., Income Tax, Advance Tax, Withholding Tax)
  6. Enter the tax period and amount
  7. Select your preferred payment mode (online banking, ATM, or over-the-counter)
  8. Click "Submit" to generate the PSID
  9. Note down or print the PSID — you will need it for the next step

The PSID remains valid for a limited period (usually 30 days). If it expires before payment, you will need to generate a new one.

Payment Method 1: Online Banking

Most major Pakistani banks support FBR tax payments through their internet banking and mobile banking platforms. The process varies slightly by bank, but generally follows these steps:

  1. Log in to your bank's internet banking or mobile app
  2. Navigate to "Bill Payment" or "Government Payments"
  3. Select "FBR" as the biller/payee
  4. Enter your PSID (the 17-digit number from the IRIS portal)
  5. Verify the amount and payment details
  6. Confirm the payment
  7. Save the transaction receipt for your records

Banks that support FBR online tax payments include:

  • HBL (Habib Bank Limited) — via HBL Mobile and Internet Banking
  • UBL (United Bank Limited) — via UBL Digital App and NetBanking
  • MCB (Muslim Commercial Bank) — via MCB Internet Banking
  • Allied Bank — via myABL and Internet Banking
  • Meezan Bank — via Meezan Mobile Banking
  • Bank Alfalah — via Alfa App and Internet Banking
  • Standard Chartered — via SC Mobile Pakistan
  • Faysal Bank — via Faysal DigiBank

Online banking payments are typically reflected in IRIS within 24-48 hours. During peak filing season (September-October), processing may take slightly longer.

Payment Method 2: Over-the-Counter (Bank Branch)

If you prefer to pay in person, you can visit any designated bank branch:

  1. Take your PSID printout or note the number
  2. Visit any branch of the designated banks (State Bank of Pakistan, NBP, HBL, UBL, MCB, ABL, and others)
  3. Request to make an FBR tax payment
  4. Provide the PSID to the teller
  5. Pay the amount in cash or through your bank account
  6. Collect the stamped payment receipt (challan)

National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) branches are the primary designated collection points for government taxes. Most other major banks also accept FBR payments at their branches.

Payment Method 3: ATM

Several banks allow FBR tax payments through their ATM networks:

  1. Insert your debit card at any ATM of a participating bank
  2. Select "Bill Payment" or "Government Payment"
  3. Select "FBR"
  4. Enter your PSID
  5. Confirm the amount and complete the transaction
  6. Keep the ATM receipt

ATM payments are convenient but may have daily transaction limits. For large tax payments, online banking or bank branch visits are more practical.

Payment Deadlines

Different types of tax payments have different deadlines:

Annual Income Tax Return

Tax must be paid before filing the annual return. The filing deadline for tax year 2025-26 is typically September 30, 2026 (often extended to October or November by the FBR).

Advance Tax Installments

If your tax liability for the year is expected to exceed PKR 200,000, you must pay advance tax in quarterly installments:

  • 1st installment: September 15 — 25% of estimated tax
  • 2nd installment: December 15 — 25% of estimated tax
  • 3rd installment: March 15 — 25% of estimated tax
  • 4th installment: June 15 — 25% of estimated tax

Late payment of advance tax installments attracts a default surcharge under Section 205 of the Income Tax Ordinance, calculated at the KIBOR rate on the shortfall amount.

Withholding Tax

Withholding agents must deposit collected withholding tax within 7 days of the end of the week in which the tax was deducted.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Wrong PSID: Double-check the 17-digit PSID before making the payment. A wrong number can credit the payment to someone else's account.
  • Wrong tax period: Make sure you select the correct tax year when generating the PSID. Payments credited to the wrong period require manual adjustment by the FBR.
  • Not saving the receipt: Always keep the payment receipt (digital or physical). Without it, proving the payment during an audit can be difficult.
  • Paying after filing: Your return should show the payment already made. Pay first, then file.
  • Ignoring advance tax: If you owe more than PKR 200,000, failing to pay in quarterly installments triggers default surcharge.

title: Withholding Tax Pakistan — All Categories & Rates 2026
excerpt: Every type of withholding tax in Pakistan explained — salary, banking, property, imports, contracts, dividends, and more. Filer vs non-filer rates.
content:
What Is Withholding Tax?

Withholding tax (WHT) is tax deducted at the source of income before it reaches you. Instead of the taxpayer paying tax directly to the FBR, the person making the payment (the withholding agent) deducts the tax and deposits it with the government on your behalf. Pakistan has one of the most extensive withholding tax regimes in the world, covering dozens of transaction categories.

Withholding taxes serve two purposes: they provide the government with a steady stream of revenue throughout the year, and they bring undocumented transactions into the tax net by collecting tax at the point of transaction.

Filer vs Non-Filer: Why It Matters

Pakistan's tax system imposes significantly higher withholding tax rates on non-filers compared to those who appear on the FBR's Active Taxpayer List (ATL). In many cases, the non-filer rate is double or even triple the filer rate.

This makes filing your tax return one of the most impactful financial decisions you can make. For more on the benefits of being an active taxpayer, see our guide on the benefits of the Active Taxpayer List.

Major Withholding Tax Categories

Section 149 — Salary Income

Every employer is required to deduct tax from employee salaries based on the applicable income tax slab rates. The employer calculates the employee's annual taxable salary, determines the tax liability, and deducts it in equal monthly installments.

  • Tax is deducted at the average rate applicable to the employee's projected annual income
  • Employers must account for tax credits, deductible allowances, and other adjustable taxes
  • Monthly tax deducted must be deposited with the FBR by the 7th of the following month

Section 151 — Profit on Debt (Banking Transactions)

Banks are required to deduct withholding tax on profit paid on deposits, savings accounts, and other debt instruments:

  • Filers: 15% on profit from debt
  • Non-filers: 30% on profit from debt

This is one of the categories where the filer/non-filer difference is most noticeable. A non-filer loses nearly a third of their bank profit to withholding tax. For more details, see our guide on withholding tax on banking transactions.

Section 153 — Payments for Goods, Services, and Contracts

This is one of the broadest withholding tax sections, covering payments made by specified persons (companies, AOPs, government entities) to suppliers:

Goods:

  • Filers: 4.5% of the gross amount
  • Non-filers: 9% of the gross amount

Services:

  • Filers: 8% of the gross amount
  • Non-filers: 16% of the gross amount

Contracts (execution of contracts):

  • Filers: 7% of the gross amount
  • Non-filers: 14% of the gross amount

For companies, these withholding taxes are generally adjustable — meaning they can be claimed as credit against the final tax liability. For individuals and AOPs in certain categories, the withholding tax may be treated as final tax (not adjustable).

Section 155 — Income from Property (Rent)

Tenants who are specified persons must deduct withholding tax on rent payments:

  • Filers: 15% of the gross rent (for commercial property)
  • Non-filers: 30% of the gross rent

For individuals receiving rental income, this withholding tax is adjustable against their total tax liability on their return.

Section 231A — Cash Withdrawal from Banks

Banks deduct withholding tax on cash withdrawals exceeding PKR 50,000 per day:

  • Filers: 0.6% of the withdrawal amount
  • Non-filers: 6% of the withdrawal amount

This is one of the starkest filer vs non-filer differences — non-filers pay 10 times the rate. This tax is adjustable for filers.

Section 231AA — Advance Tax on Transactions with Banks

This section covers various banking transactions including demand drafts, pay orders, and other instruments:

  • Filers: 0.6% of the transaction amount
  • Non-filers: 6% of the transaction amount

Section 236 — Telephone and Internet Services

Telecom companies deduct advance tax on mobile phone bills and prepaid recharges:

  • Filers: 15% of the bill amount (including sales tax)
  • Non-filers: 25% of the bill amount

This tax can be claimed as adjustable in your annual return. For instructions on obtaining certificates, see our guides on downloading tax certificates from Telenor and PTCL.

Section 236C — Advance Tax on Sale/Transfer of Immovable Property

When immovable property is sold or transferred, the buyer is required to collect advance tax from the seller:

  • Filers: 3% of the property value (as per FBR valuation table)
  • Non-filers: 10.5% of the property value

For property purchases (Section 236K), the buyer also pays advance tax:

  • Filers: 3% of the property value
  • Non-filers: 10.5% of the property value

The difference between filer and non-filer rates on property transactions is enormous and can amount to hundreds of thousands or even millions of rupees on a single transaction.

Section 236H — Advance Tax on Purchase of Motor Vehicles

Tax is collected at the time of registration or transfer of motor vehicles:

  • Rates vary by engine capacity and whether the buyer is a filer or non-filer
  • For vehicles up to 850cc: Filer PKR 10,000 / Non-filer PKR 25,000
  • For vehicles 851-1000cc: Filer PKR 20,000 / Non-filer PKR 50,000
  • For vehicles 1001-1300cc: Filer PKR 25,000 / Non-filer PKR 75,000
  • For vehicles 1301-1600cc: Filer PKR 50,000 / Non-filer PKR 150,000
  • For vehicles 1601-1800cc: Filer PKR 75,000 / Non-filer PKR 200,000
  • For vehicles 1801-2000cc: Filer PKR 100,000 / Non-filer PKR 300,000
  • For vehicles above 2000cc: Filer PKR 150,000 / Non-filer PKR 450,000

How to Claim Adjustable Withholding Taxes

Most withholding taxes in Pakistan are adjustable, meaning they can be credited against your final income tax liability when you file your annual return. Here is how to claim them:

  1. Collect certificates and statements: Obtain withholding tax certificates from all sources — banks, employers, telecom companies, property buyers/sellers, etc.
  2. Verify amounts on IRIS: Log in to the FBR IRIS portal and check your withholding tax credit statement. All taxes deducted against your CNIC/NTN should appear here.
  3. Report in your tax return: Enter each withholding tax amount in the appropriate section of your income tax return on IRIS.
  4. Calculate the difference: If your total withholding taxes exceed your final tax liability, you are entitled to a refund. If they fall short, you must pay the balance.

It is critical to verify that all withholding taxes have been correctly reported against your NTN/CNIC. Discrepancies are common, especially with telecom tax and banking tax deductions.

Final Tax vs Adjustable Tax

Understanding this distinction is essential:

  • Adjustable (minimum) tax: The withholding tax is a credit against your annual tax liability. If your total tax exceeds the withholding, you pay the difference. If the withholding exceeds your tax, you claim a refund. Most withholding taxes are adjustable for filers.
  • Final tax: The withholding tax IS your total tax liability for that income. You do not need to include that income in your annual return, and you cannot claim a refund on it. Certain categories of income for non-filers and specific sections are treated as final tax.
